origins: This belief usually comes from betrayal: a parent who broke promises, abuse by someone who should have protected us, a spouse’s unfaithfulness, gossip, or being cheated. After being hurt, it makes sense to protect ourselves. But when the lesson becomes “no one can ever be trusted,” we can end up isolated, suspicious, and unable to receive the support we need.
teaches: Scripture is realistic about people. It warns that it is better to take refuge in the Lord than to trust in man, and Jesus told His followers to be shrewd as snakes and innocent as doves. Wisdom means trusting carefully, not blindly. But the Bible also calls us into community, forgiveness, and love. Our full trust belongs to God, who never fails. Because He is trustworthy, we can risk measured trust with people, give it gradually, and watch whether it is honored.
self_statements: If I trust, I’ll get hurt.
I can only count on myself.
It’s safer to keep everyone at arm’s length.
errors: Deciding everyone is untrustworthy because some people betrayed me.
Believing I must either trust completely or not at all.
Assuming people have bad motives without evidence.
questions: Who betrayed my trust, and what did I learn from it?
Is there anyone who has proven trustworthy over time?
Can I trust someone a little without trusting them with everything?
What signs show that a person is trustworthy?
What does God say about where my full trust belongs?
What small risk of trust could I take with a safe person?
truth: Some people have betrayed me, and I am wise to be careful. But not everyone is untrustworthy. My full trust belongs to God, who never fails. Because I am secure in Him, I can offer trust to people gradually and wisely, and watch whether it is honored.
hw_truths: When I am afraid, I can trust God.
Wisdom means trusting carefully, not never.
Trust can be built step by step.
Forgiving does not require trusting blindly.
log: Each day, write one small way you trusted someone and whether that trust was honored.
actions: List small, medium, and large things you could trust someone with. Start with one small item this week.
Write the names of people who have kept their word to you, even in small things.
With a new person, look for consistency between words and actions over time before deciding.
If betrayal or abuse still feels raw, talk with a counselor or pastor about healing and safe boundaries.
prayer: Lord, I have been hurt by people I trusted. Thank You that You are completely trustworthy. Heal my wounds, give me wisdom to see who is safe, and courage to trust carefully again. Amen.
